version.changelog: Added all platform scripts: Instagram, YouTube, Meta, video generation. Removed hardcoded branding — now uses configurable BRAND_URL/BRAND_NAME placeholders.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement full social posting automation, but the manifest, runtime instructions, and code disagree about which credentials and services are required — several mismatches and omissions increase risk and deserve manual review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim exactly what the code implements (posting to X, Instagram, YouTube, Meta, video generation). However the published registry metadata says 'no required env vars' while SKILL.md and the code expect many secrets (X, IG, META tokens). The code also references Cloudflare R2 and YouTube config files not declared in SKILL.md or registry metadata. This inconsistency (metadata says no secrets; runtime requires many) is unexplained and therefore concerning.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs full autonomous posting, scheduling via GitHub Actions, and to place API keys in .env — which matches the bot's behavior. But SKILL.md's declared required env vars omit other environment variables the code reads (R2_* values, INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET, and likely YouTube credentials in omitted files). The instructions encourage storing secrets for automated posting (GitHub Actions cron), which is normal for this class of tool but raises operational risk if secrets are not scoped or stored securely.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (no installer URL or package), which lowers one class of risk. But the code uses many heavy Python packages (moviepy, html2image, numpy, PIL, requests, dotenv) and there is no dependency manifest listed in the package metadata. The absence of an install/dependency declaration means users may need to install runtime libraries manually and the skill may fail or require privileging to satisfy native dependencies.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md asks for multiple high-privilege posting credentials (X, Instagram, Meta). That is proportionate for a posting automation. However the code expects additional environment variables not listed in SKILL.md (Cloudflare R2: R2_ENDPOINT, R2_ACCESS_KEY, R2_SECRET_KEY, R2_BUCKET, R2_PUBLIC_URL; INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET; and references to YouTube config). Those missing declarations are an incoherence — the skill will need credentials beyond what the docs promise. Requesting full posting tokens is sensitive: ensure tokens have minimal scopes and are dedicated test accounts when evaluating.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). Model invocation is allowed (default), so the skill can act autonomously if the agent chooses to invoke it. That is expected for a posting automation, but combined with the many required posting credentials it increases the blast radius if the skill or the agent is compromised. The SKILL.md suggests running scheduled GitHub Actions which would store secrets in CI; that operational choice should be reviewed carefully.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Do not install blindly. Things to check before using:

1) Credentials and gaps: SKILL.md and the registry metadata disagree — the code requires additional env vars (Cloudflare R2 keys, INSTAGRAM_APP_SECRET, likely YouTube credentials) that are not declared in the registry. Ask the author for a complete list of required environment variables and why each is needed. Refuse to provide high-privilege production tokens until you can test safely.

2) Use least-privilege test accounts: Create dedicated/test social accounts and tokens with minimal scopes (only posting) for initial evaluation. Never use your primary accounts until you verify behavior.

3) Review missing/omitted files: instagram_main imports bot.r2_uploader and there are truncated/omitted files — inspect r2_uploader.py and yt_config.py before running. Search code for any hard-coded remote endpoints or unexpected network calls.

4) Dependency & runtime safety: The package lacks an install/dependency manifest. Install it in an isolated environment (disposable VM or container), run the skill in --dry-run mode, and verify it does not send credentials or data to unknown endpoints.

5) GitHub Actions guidance: If you follow the scheduling advice, store secrets in GitHub Secrets with minimal scopes and enable repository protection and secret rotation. Consider avoiding storing long-lived tokens in shared CI.

6) Data handling and public URLs: The code uploads generated videos to Cloudflare R2 and may set public URLs (R2_PUBLIC_URL). Confirm whether uploaded content is publicly accessible and whether that matches your privacy/brand requirements.

7) Monitor and limit: When you first enable posting, monitor logs, set rate limits, and keep automatic posting disabled until you are confident in generated content. Verify comment/reply behavior to avoid accidental policy-violating posts.

Given the multiple mismatches between manifest, documentation, and code, treat this skill as suspicious until the author clarifies the missing env vars and you audit the omitted uploader/config files.
